The Geo Metro Convertible is one of the silliest cars ever sold in America. The Metro hatchback was already a misfit on American roads, with its microscopic 1.0-liter three-cylinder engine, 1,600-pound curb weight, and $7,000-ish starting price. It was a General Motors rebadge of a Suzuki Swift, and it almost immediately became the butt of every automotive joke. There was no logical reason, then, for any engineer to lop off its roof and turn it into a convertible, but that didn't stop it from happening, and honestly I'm grateful GM sold them anyway. I doubt GM ever imagined that a YouTuber would end up driving one from New York to Los Angeles 34 years after it was built, but that's just what Mitchell Kohrmann did in his latest video .

When new, the Geo Metro convertible was fabled to have 55 horsepower and 58 pound-feet of torque, but Kohrmann was smart enough to dyno test his remarkably clean 1992 Metro convertible before setting off on his cross-continental journey. Before that, though, he gave it a tune-up and fixed the air conditioning — or at least he thought he did... After a 50-second pull, the dyno showed the Metro made 43 horsepower and 53 lb-ft of torque. That's more than enough to complete a 2,838-mile road trip that includes a 10,000-foot climb, right?

There's never a guarantee a startup car company will actually make it. Automotive history is littered with companies that never made it more than a few years, and after some of Rivian's early financial troubles, it wasn't out of the question that the Irvine, California-based company could join that group. Well, following the introduction of the R2 , those fears seem to be all but squashed.

Rivian just posted its third-quarter results for 2026, and the compact-crossover-sized R2 helped raise the automaker's deliveries by 46% year-over-year to 19,248 vehicles, according to Car and Driver . That means Rivian is increasing its yearly sales projection to between 67,000 and 70,000 vehicles — up from 65,000 to 70,000. It also just so happened to outsell the larger and more expensive R1S and R1T flagships combined, as well as the EDV delivery van. I should note that Rivian didn't explicitly say how many R2s it sold, though. This news comes even though the only R2 that Rivian currently sells is the most expensive Performance version of the electric SUV, and the idea that Rivian is still "early in the ramp" of R2 production, according to CEO RJ Scaringe, who spoke with Reuters .

item.dc:creator: Marco Rossi
item.description: Loading a truck can be tricky if the cargo is heavy or awkward, like with a motorcycle. Tesla might have a novel solution, based on a patent application published a week ago that puts the trick suspension system in the Cybertruck — including the new low-cost model — to work.

Loading a truck can be tricky if the cargo is heavy or awkward, like with a motorcycle. Tesla might have a novel solution, based on a patent application published a week ago that puts the trick suspension system in the Cybertruck — including the new low-cost model — to work. At the owner's command, it would raise the front of the truck, lower the rear, and make access to the bed that much easier. Patent application number US 2026/0326744 A1, titled 'Adjustable Suspension For A Vehicle', details a 'ramp mode' that independently adjusts the suspension at each wheel.

The drawings use the familiar wedge-shaped pickup, but it's worth noting that Tesla describes the technology broadly rather than exclusively for the Cybertruck. Tilting the truck changes the angle where a ramp would meet the bed, which could make loading an ATV or motorcycle easier. Tesla also says lowering the rear would allow owners to use a shorter ramp. In one example, the automaker proposes raising the front of the truck by 80 mm (3.1 inches) while lowering the rear by 70 mm (2.8 inches) to reduce the ramp-to-bed breakover angle.

For the first time since 1953, an Italian is the F1 World Drivers' Champion. Kimi Antonelli finished third at the Mexico City Grand Prix on Sunday, clinching the championship. The 20-year-old Mercedes driver also became F1's youngest-ever champion, surpassing the mark set by a 23-year-old Sebastian Vettel in 2010. With Antonelli never crossing the finish line lower than fifth so far this season, the ninth-place finish he needed to secure his maiden title seemed like a cakewalk. However, nothing is ever guaranteed in Formula 1.

Antonelli was never in contention for the win at Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez , but that didn't matter. His main goal was getting home in one piece. The young Italian qualified fourth and stayed there before cycling to the lead during the pit stop. He would eventually have to yield the position to make his own stop on Lap 43. He could've held the lead if he stayed out on lap longer. Valtteri Bottas' Cadillac suffered a catastrophic left-front suspension failure while heading into Turn 1. The machine became a sled, slid through the run-off area and slammed into the barrier. It took a while for Bottas to get out of the cockpit, but he walked away. Race control was forced to throw a red flag to recover his car.

The Chevrolet Corvette has been Detroit's answer to the European sports car for more than seventy years. Since 1953, it has gone through eight distinct generations. The idea behind the Corvette came from Harley Earl, former head of design at General Motors, who envisioned an affordable two-seat roadster that could stand beside the imports returning stateside with World War II veterans. The first Corvette shipped with a six-cylinder engine, and it was Zora Arkus-Duntov (later nicknamed the " Father of the Corvette ") who pushed the car towards the V8 power it would become known for.

From there, the Corvette never stopped evolving. The front-engine layout that defined the nameplate for decades was finally abandoned when the eighth generation arrived with its engine behind the driver, a change that purists argued about — and the stopwatch quietly settled. What makes the Corvette so interesting is that it has always been judged by two audiences. One cares about straight-line muscle and badge pride. The other, which is usually more critical, cares about how a car handles when the road bends. And for a car built to take on Porsche, Jaguar, and Ferrari, that second audience matters just as much as the first — if not more.

Volkswagen's solution was a special manual gearbox design where the final shift gate was marked with a capital 'E'.

The '3+E' and '4+E' setups found in the original VW Golf , Jetta, and the U.S.-spec Rabbit models had nothing to do with electrification. Many drivers at the time understandably assumed that the letter stood for 'Economy' or an 'Extra' gear. However, Volkswagen documents confirm that the magic word is 'Efficiency'. Rather than being a new designation for the fourth or fifth gears, the 'E' slot engaged an overdrive designed to lower engine speeds, minimize wear, and improve the fuel economy ratings at highway speeds.

At the core of this thinking is the fact that the IRS does not distinguish between fuel choices, so there’s no separate depreciation category for electric- vs. diesel-fueled commercial trucks. The relevant classifications, then, are the vehicle’s use and property classes, and under the IRS’ depreciation guidelines, tractor units designed for over-the-road use are classified as 3-year properties and fall under the 20-year recovery threshold for 100% bonus depreciation, Tesla’s electric Semi can benefit from 179 just like their diesel-powered competitors. But don’t get me wrong – this isn’t just great news for Tesla Semi buyers. Electric garbage trucks , electric vocational trucks , battery electric reefer trailers , and even some big electric forklifts can potentially benefit from the same accelerated depreciation rules, since the IRS lists these as, “specialized business vehicles,” with no distinction between electric, diesel, natural gas, hydrogen , magic pixie dust, anything else.
